item.title: Bridging Theory and Practice in Sustainability Marketing
item.content:encoded:
A. R. Shaheen Hosany, Hult International Business School

Seongsoo Jang, Cardiff University

The escalating environmental crisis is reshaping consumer behaviour across food, fashion, entertainment and travel. Despite widespread awareness of sustainability issues, consumers struggle to translate their environmental values into consistent sustainable practices due to affordability, convenience, infrastructure and competing priorities constraints. This special issue seeks research that moves beyond examining intentions and attitudes to investigate how sustainability is actually enacted and experienced in real-world contexts.

The gap between sustainability theory and practice presents an opportunity for meaningful knowledge creation. Researchers are encouraged to explore how sustainability challenges can inform theoretical development while rigorous theory can guide practitioners in designing effective interventions. The issue welcomes diverse methodological approaches including qualitative, quantitative, experimental and mixed-methods research that illuminates the lived realities of sustainable consumption and examines the role of marketing in enabling genuine behavioural and systemic change.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Consumers, everyday practices and sustainability transitions - How climate vulnerability reshapes consumer identities, aspirations, routines, lifestyles and consumption practices
  • How social influence, norms, communities and cultural contexts shape environmental sustainability
  • Consumer willingness to sacrifice and pay for sustainability, and cost distribution across stakeholders
  • Environmental constraints stimulating repair, reuse, sharing and non-consumption
  • Emerging forms of consumption, access, sharing, circularity and non-consumption
  • Firms, brands, innovation and circular consumption - Translating sustainability theory into products, services and business models
  • Designing products and systems that make sustainable practices feasible, affordable and convenient
  • Marketing strategy enabling repair, reuse, circular consumption and product life extension
  • Marketing contributing to systemic change rather than individual consumer responsibility
  • Sustainability, inequality and systemic transformation - Moving beyond individual behavioural change to systemic transformation
  • Cost distribution of sustainability transitions across stakeholders
  • How inequalities shape consumer capacity for sustainability participation
  • Marketing contribution to sustainability policy design and evaluation
  • Digital technologies, marketing communications and behavioural change - Digital technologies and AI facilitating sustainable consumption transitions
  • Social media, influencers and digital platforms shaping sustainability perceptions and behaviours
  • Digital marketing enabling behavioural change without increasing burden or manipulation
  • Creating conditions enabling sustainable behaviour beyond persuasion
  • Real-world evidence, experimental research and methodological approaches - Using transaction data and behavioural datasets to reveal actual consumption
  • Causal impact of sustainability marketing interventions on consumer behaviour
  • Natural experiments using climate disruptions and environmental regulations
  • Data-driven discovery using digital and computational data
  • Mixed-methods approaches integrating qualitative, quantitative and real-world data

Timeline

  • September 20, 2027: Submissions open
  • December 20, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: Human Centred AI in Strategic Decision Making
item.content:encoded:
Shahriar Akter, University of Wollongong

Carolyn Strong, Cardiff University

Marketing is experiencing rapid transformation through AI adoption, yet over 80% of AI initiatives fail to deliver expected financial returns. Despite most CMOs experimenting with AI, fewer than 10% have successfully scaled it across marketing workflows. The gap between AI potential and actual value creation highlights the need for marketing processes centered on humans orchestrating AI, channels, and personalization as a continuous growth engine.

This special issue seeks high-quality research examining how human-centered AI can enhance strategic decision-making in marketing. It welcomes papers addressing responsible AI principles such as beneficence, autonomy, security, justice, and explicability, alongside practical challenges in marketing-specific AI governance, security risks in autonomous agents, algorithmic bias mitigation, and the reskilling of marketing teams for effective human-AI collaboration.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Continuous insights: Using multiple data sources for segmentation, campaign execution, and analytics with AI collaboration to predict consumer behaviours
  • Security in Agentic creativity: Addressing data breaches, cyberattacks, and security risks in agentic AI systems, including automatic campaign scaling and optimization
  • Trust and algorithmic biases: Implementing auditing protocols to identify and correct distortions in data and models
  • AI governance and ethical principles: Establishing AI governance frameworks and marketing-specific ethical guidelines for socially beneficial AI adoption
  • Human-centred marketing skills: Reskilling and upskilling marketing talent in data analytics, hyper-personalisation, chatbots, and virtual assistants for strategic decision-making
  • AI failures: Understanding why AI projects fail due to data quality, customer needs identification, expectations management, and cultural readiness in human-AI collaboration

Timeline

  • October 30, 2026: Abstract deadline
  • March 31, 2027: Manuscript deadline

item.title: New-age Technologies Driven Strategic Marketing for a Better World
item.content:encoded:
Chiara Civera, University of Turin

Demetris Vrontis, University of Nicosia

Sanjit K. Roy, Edith Cowan University

Valentina Chiaudano, University of Turin

The special issue examines how emerging technologies like artificial intelligence, machine learning, and blockchain can reshape marketing strategies toward a multi-stakeholder approach in global contexts. While firms increasingly deploy advanced technologies to enhance customer engagement and personalization, there is limited understanding of how these technologies can support marketing that simultaneously addresses the interests of employees, suppliers, regulators, communities, and society. The issue seeks to bridge this gap by exploring how NATs enable stakeholder engagement, value creation, and governance across global marketing ecosystems.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Lire l'appel complet sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Artificial Intelligence and Value Co-Creation in Global Marketing Ecosystems: how AI and advanced technologies reshape marketing strategies, processes, and interactions among multiple stakeholders in global markets; how NATs enable new forms of value co-creation among firms, customers, suppliers, regulators, and communities; how technology-enabled marketing infrastructures enhance transparency and coordination across global value chains
  • Governance, Ethics, and Responsible AI in Marketing: ethical, governance, and organizational implications of NAT-driven marketing systems; algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, and fairness in data-driven marketing practices; governance mechanisms and organizational capabilities for implementing responsible and transparent NAT-enabled marketing strategies; managing stakeholder tensions and trade-offs arising from NAT-supported marketing decisions
  • Cross-Country Dynamics of New-age Technologies in Marketing: how institutional environments, cultural contexts, and regulatory frameworks influence the adoption and governance of artificial intelligence in global marketing; cross-country differences in implementation of NAT-enabled marketing strategies; how new-age technologies influence global marketing strategy and ecosystem coordination; how NATs support sustainable, inclusive, and responsible marketing practices in global markets

Timeline

  • April 30, 2027: Manuscript submission deadline

item.title: AI-driven marketing and Sustainability
item.content:encoded:
Pham Van Hau, Unitec Institute of Technology

Carolyn Strong, Cardiff University

Park Thaichon, University of Southern Queensland

This special issue focuses on the emerging intersection of artificial intelligence and sustainable marketing. AI technologies like machine learning and predictive analytics are rapidly transforming marketing practices, while sustainability challenges demand new approaches to shift consumption patterns and market systems. The special issue seeks research examining how AI-driven marketing influences sustainability outcomes at individual, organizational, and system-wide levels.

The integration of AI in marketing presents both opportunities and challenges for sustainability. AI tools can enable personalized sustainability nudges, improve resource efficiency, and support circular economy initiatives. However, concerns include algorithmic bias, privacy issues, transparency challenges, and the risk of reinforcing unsustainable consumption through hyper-personalized marketing. Understanding these dynamics is critical to ensure AI contributes positively to sustainable futures rather than exacerbating environmental and social challenges.

item.title: Strategic Marketing and Regenerative Futures
item.content:encoded:
Ninh Nguyen, RMIT University

Ranjit Voola, The University of Sydney

M S Balaji, RMIT University

Dung Minh Nguyen, National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology

Carolyn Strong, Cardiff University

This special issue examines how strategic marketing can advance regenerative futures. While sustainability remains important, regenerative approaches go beyond harm reduction and efficiency to actively restore social, ecological, and economic systems through business strategies, partnerships, and market practices. The issue seeks to understand how firms formulate regenerative marketing goals, develop and communicate regenerative strategies, and align commercial objectives with societal and ecological renewal.

The call invites both conceptual and empirical research exploring marketing's role in enabling restoration, renewal, resilience, and long-term stakeholder value creation. Diverse methodologies are welcome, including experiments, surveys, qualitative research, mixed methods, and multi-level or cross-cultural approaches. Papers should address strategic marketing capabilities, brand strategy, consumer behaviour, digital marketing, business models, stakeholder collaboration, and evaluation metrics related to regenerative transformation.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Strategic marketing capabilities for a regenerative future
  • Regenerative marketing strategy and long-term value creation
  • Brand strategy, brand purpose, and regenerative value propositions
  • Consumer behaviour in relation to regenerative offerings and marketing implications
  • Digital and social media marketing for regenerative transformation
  • The role of emerging technologies in enabling regenerative marketing strategies
  • Leveraging AI and big data for regenerative strategic marketing
  • Market shaping and ecosystem orchestration for regenerative futures
  • Circular, restorative, and regenerative business models from a strategic marketing perspective
  • Strategic partnerships and cross-sector collaborations for regenerative value creation
  • The role of communities, stakeholders, and co-creation in regenerative marketing
  • Metrics, accountability, and performance evaluation in regenerative marketing strategy
  • Marketing ethics, governance, and regulations related to regenerative claims and practices

  • Strategies for inclusive restoration in emerging markets
  • Strategic marketing and regenerative futures at the Base of the Pyramid

item.title: Strategic Marketing, Technology, and Societal Transformation: Ethics, Power, and Social Change
item.content:encoded:
Reem Khamis Hamdan, The University College of Bahrain

Marketing has evolved beyond economic value creation to encompass broader social impacts, particularly as digital technologies like artificial intelligence and big data become deeply embedded in society. These advancements enable marketing strategies that influence not only consumer behavior but also societal values and well-being, raising critical questions about ethical implications and power dynamics that remain underexplored in academic literature.

This special issue invites research examining how strategic marketing enabled by technology reshapes society and the accompanying ethical and power concerns. The editors seek both theoretical and empirical contributions that illuminate the relationship between marketing strategies and society, with particular emphasis on ethical issues, power imbalances, and societal consequences of marketing in digital environments.

Appel publié par Journal of Strategic Marketing. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Ethical concerns of AI marketing
  • Bias and fairness of marketing algorithms
  • Digital surveillance and the privacy of consumers
  • Power relations and manipulation of consumers by digital marketing
  • Social responsibility of influencer marketing
  • Mental health/well-being of consumers
  • Multidisciplinary marketing and digital inequality

  • Social responsibility of marketing and ESG
  • Multidisciplinary marketing of brands
  • Multidisciplinary marketing in vulnerable communities
  • Multidisciplinary marketing of technology and the transformation of the identity of consumers
  • Multidisciplinary marketing of the attention economy
